headline: NMDC commissions Rs 5,427 crore Iron ore processing plant,
fullText:
Ministry of Steel

NMDC commissions Rs 5,427 crore Iron ore processing plant,

slurry pipeline and pellet plant in Bastar, Chhattisgarh

27 SEP 2026 11:48PM by PIB Delhi

NMDC Ltd has commissioned its 2 million tonne per annum (MTPA) pellet plant at Nagarnar in Chhattisgarh, as part of a Rs 5,427-crore integrated project of iron ore processing, pipeline and pellet making connecting its iron ore operations at Bacheli with the company's steel plant at Nagarnar.

The project includes a new iron ore processing plant at Bacheli, a 15 MTPA slurry pipeline and the 2 MTPA pellet plant at Nagarnar. The 135 km slurry pipeline carries processed iron ore concentrate from Bacheli to Nagarnar, providing an alternative to transporting the material by road.

The maiden production from the pellet plant was monitored live from NMDC's headquarters by Chairman and Managing Director Amitava Mukherjee and the company's senior leadership, as adverse weather conditions prevented them from travelling to the project site.

The facilities will enable NMDC to process iron ore fines and slimes from its Bailadila mines into concentrate and subsequently convert the concentrate into pellets. The pellet plant uses Straight Grate Induration technology to produce pellets for use in steelmaking.

"Today is a day of immense pride for everyone at NMDC. This has not been an easy project to execute. It involved the processing facilities, the actual slurry pipeline and the pellet plant. But today is a red-letter day—a day we have been waiting for a long time. This is the day when our collective dream is coming true," Amitava Mukherjee, Chairman and Managing Director, NMDC Ltd., said.

The commissioning strengthens NMDC's presence across the iron ore value chain, from mining and beneficiation to slurry transportation and pellet production. It also adds a new value-added product to the company's portfolio and allows it to make greater use of iron ore fines and slimes generated from its Bailadila operations.

The project is part of NMDC's broader expansion and diversification strategy as the company works towards increasing its iron ore production capacity to 100 million tonnes in the long term.

The slurry pipeline passes through 61 villages in Bastar and Dantewada districts and is designed to reduce the movement of processed ore by road, provide alternate mode of evacuation and lower dependency on Railways and ensures a dedicated link between NMDC's Bacheli operations and Nagarnar.

headline: Green Highways
fullText:
PIB Backgrounder

India's Journey Towards Sustainable Road Infrastructure

28 SEP 2026 6:30PM by PIB Delhi

India’s green highway approach is transforming road infrastructure through plantation, climate-resilient design and resource-efficient construction. Over the last five years, more than 3.61 crore saplings have been planted across approximately 1.32 lakh km of National Highways. From Miyawaki forests to recycled construction materials and indigenous bio-bitumen technology, green practices are shaping highway development. Satellite-based monitoring through the National Highways Green Cover Index is strengthening scientific assessment of green cover. Community initiatives and pollinator corridors are also adding a wider ecological dimension.

Building Roads, Growing Green

India’s highways are no longer just corridors of connectivity. They are becoming an important part of the country’s broader infrastructure transformation. As road infrastructure expands, the focus is also shifting towards building corridors that are efficient, resilient and environmentally responsible.

Over the past decade, India’s National Highway network has grown by nearly 61%, from 91,287 km in 2014 to 1,46,572 km by March 2026. This rapid development has strengthened connectivity, improved access to markets and supported faster movement of people and goods. As road infrastructure expands, the focus is also shifting towards building corridors that are efficient, resilient and environmentally responsible. Large-scale plantation along National Highways (NH), the use of recycled and waste-derived materials, energy-efficient construction practices, and satellite-based monitoring of green cover are contributing to a more sustainable highway network.

Green Highways Policy, 2015: Policy Evolution

The greening of India’s National Highway network is guided by the Green Highways (Plantation, Transplantation, Beautification and Maintenance) Policy, 2015. The Policy was formulated to:

Evolve a policy framework for plantation along National Highways.

Reduce the impact of air pollution and dust, as trees and shrubs are known to be natural sinks for air pollutants.

Arrest soil erosion at the embankment slopes.

Moderate the effect of wind and incoming radiation.

Create employment opportunities for local people.

The implementation of the policy brings together multiple stakeholders. Plantation activities are undertaken by Self Help Groups, private agencies, State Forest Departments, Forest Corporations and contractors, according to the scope of sanctioned works. A Plantation Cell has been established for overall monitoring through regional offices of the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) and other agencies.

Greening the Corridors: Plantation & Afforestation

The greening of National Highways is increasingly being measured by the number of saplings planted, their survival, growth and distribution along highway corridors. As of July 2026, more than 3.61 crore saplings have been planted across approximately 1.32 lakh km of National Highways during the last five years. The approach has also expanded from plantation to broader environmental management. Earlier, monitoring of plantations relied primarily on site visits by field personnel. Today, this is being supplemented by drone and satellite based monitoring. Miyawaki plantations have also been introduced to increase green cover. Wherever tree felling is necessary for highway development, compensatory afforestation and tree transplantation are being undertaken.

The Miyawaki technique is a method of creating dense forests within limited spaces. Also known as the ‘pot plantation method’, it involves planting trees and shrubs close to one another to promote rapid growth and establish forest-like ecosystems in a shorter period. Plants can grow up to 10 times faster under this method, making it particularly suitable for expanding green cover in space-constrained urban areas.

Plantation and landscaping have become an integral part of National Highway development and project completion. NHAI’s September 2026 guidelines reinforce this approach. Plantation works will be considered compliant for provisional completion certification only when at least 80% of the available Right of Way (RoW) earmarked for plantation has been covered. RoW refers to the designated land area that is legally required for the construction, operation, and maintenance of highway infrastructure. The planted saplings must also have a minimum 90% survival rate at the time of inspection by officials. The same survival benchmark applies during the Operations and Maintenance period, with provisions for timely replacement of plants that do not survive.

To encourage good practices, NHAI instituted the Green Highways Excellence Awards in 2025. The 2026 awards placed the highest weightage on plantation survival, along with species diversity, use of native species, site-specific plans and protection measures.

In the Avenue Plantations category, the Six-Laning of the Chilakaluripet Bypass on NH-16 in Andhra Pradesh secured the First Prize.

In the Median Plantations category, the Four-Laning of the Hyderabad–Yadgiri section of NH-163was awarded the First Prize.

The Jamtha Clover Leaf Oxygen Bird Park on NH-44,Nagpur, received the First Prize in the Plantation in Land Parcels category.

These award-winning efforts show how every stretch of a highway can become an opportunity to add greenery and strengthen the surrounding landscape.

National Highways – Green Cover Index (NH-GCI) Marking a new milestone in sustainable highway development, the first Annual Report on the National Highways Green Cover Index (NH-GCI) 2025–26 has been released. Prepared in collaboration with the National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC) of ISRO, the report provides the country's first scientific and quantitative assessment of green cover within the RoW along National Highways. The assessment covers nearly 30,000 kilometres of National Highways under the Operation and Maintenance (O&M) phase across 24 states. It includes observations recorded before and after the monsoon season. Using advanced space-based technologies, it establishes a reliable baseline for monitoring and enhancing roadside plantations. The assessment reveals significant variation in green cover along National Highways. The findings enable comparison, ranking, and targeted interventions for improved plantation management.

Driving the Shift to Sustainable Materials

India’s highways are also transitioning from fossil-fuel-based materials towards bio-based, regenerative solutions. A major scientific breakthrough was announced in January 2026 with the technology transfer of Bio-Bitumen produced via pyrolysis of farm residue. Technology transfer (TT) is a process that allows scientific findings, knowledge and intellectual property to flow from universities and research institutions to public and private users.

The innovation, “Bio-Bitumen via Pyrolysis: From Farm Residue to Roads”, was developed jointly by CSIR-Central Road Research Institute (CSIR-CRRI), New Delhi, and CSIR-Indian Institute of Petroleum (CSIR-IIP), Dehradun. Bitumen is a mixture of organic liquids and hydrocarbons, used for paving roads, and is known as black gold in the pavement industry. Currently, India meets nearly 50% of its bitumen requirement through imports. Innovations such as bio-bitumen can reduce import dependence while strengthening domestic production capabilities.

The process uses post-harvest rice straw as feedstock for producing bio-oil through pyrolysis.

The bio-oil is subsequently blended with conventional bitumen to produce the bio-bitumen blend. The technology uses biomass pyrolysis to produce multiple value streams, including bio-binders for roads, energy-efficient gaseous fuel, bio-pesticide fractions and high-grade carbon. These outputs have applications in batteries, water purification and advanced materials, offering an emission-free and cost-effective solution for the future.

A 100-metre trial stretch using bio-bitumen has been successfully laid on the Jorabat–Shillong Expressway (NH-40) in Meghalaya, demonstrating its feasibility. The technology also supports management of farm residue. Plans are underway to integrate this into national highway construction standards. With this, India has emerged as the first country to scale bio-bitumen technology to industrial and commercial levels within the same year.

The shift towards alternative materials is also visible in the wider use of recycled and industrial by-products in highway construction. Fly ash, a thermal power plant by-product, and pond ash are increasingly used in embankments and structural works. Reclaimed Asphalt Pavement (RAP), Construction and Demolition (C&D) waste and recycled aggregates are also used in suitable highway works, as per technical specifications. Other materials being promoted include plastic waste, slag, crumb rubber, bio-bitumen and other recycled or industrial by-products. Together, these practices improve resource efficiency, conserve natural resources and help address environmental concerns associated with highway construction.

Community Engagement & Public Awareness

The impact of green highway initiatives is most visible on the ground, where plantations are being linked with biodiversity and community participation. Experiences from different States show how highway spaces can become platforms for wider environmental action.

Turning Highway Greenery into Pollinator Corridors

Green corridors along highways can serve purposes beyond shade and landscape improvement. Along identified stretches of the Delhi-Amritsar-Katra Expressway, pollinator corridors under the “Trees for Bees” campaign are being developed. The initiative uses flowering and locally suitable species to provide nectar and pollen across seasons, creating continuous habitat for bees and other pollinators.

Sustaining the Green Cover

Andhra Pradesh has seen sustained plantation activity along its National Highway network. Between 2010 and 2025, around 18 lakh seedlings were planted through avenue and median plantations. These plantations are being maintained to mitigate the adverse impacts of climate change and ensure safer travel for highway users.

For 2026–27, a further 3.86 lakh saplings have been targeted for avenue and median plantation across the State. On World Environment Day 2026, around 3,200 saplings were planted across Andhra Pradesh under the “Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam” initiative.

Together, these efforts reflect a shift from planting trees along highways to nurturing green corridors that communities can help sustain over time.

Building the Highways of Tomorrow

India’s highway sector today stands at the intersection of large-scale infrastructure delivery and environmental stewardship. Each initiative, from grassroots plantation to indigenous bio-bitumen, reflects a common thread. Growth need not come at the expense of green cover. The Green Highways story is woven into India’s larger national priorities. These span climate action, self-reliance and inclusive growth. It reinforces the vision of Viksit Bharat through sustainable, technology-backed infrastructure. As India’s highway network expands, its green cover is expanding alongside it.

headline: Department of Food and Public Distribution Continues Swachhata Hi Seva-2026 Campaign with Cleanliness Drives and Public Awareness Activities
fullText:
Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution

Department of Food and Public Distribution Continues Swachhata Hi Seva-2026 Campaign with Cleanliness Drives and Public Awareness Activities

DFPD Promotes Cleanliness, Hygiene and Community Participation through Swachhata Hi Seva-2026

DFPD Organises Door-to-Door Awareness Campaign, Walkathon and Plogging Drive to Promote Cleanliness

28 SEP 2026 6:28PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Food and Public Distribution (DFPD), Government of India, including all its PSUs, attached/ subordinate offices are conducting activities under ‘Swachhata Hi Seva-2026’ campaign as per guidelines of Department of Urban Development and Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation for the cleanliness and sanitation.

The DFPD organized a door-to-door awareness campaign at Firoz Gandhi Camp, New Delhi on 21.09.2026. The officials of the department visited the camp and distributed brooms, dustbins, soaps, sanitizers to the residents of the camp. The officers briefed the residents about the importance of not only keeping their houses but also their surroundings clean. The children of the residents were also sensitized about personal hygiene and keeping their environment clean.

The DFPD organized a spirited Walkathon & Plogging Drive from Krishi Bhawan to Jantar Mantar on 22.09. 2026.The event inspired citizens to embrace cleanliness and reaffirmed commitment to a Swachh Bharat.

Swachhata Samvad, a cleanliness dialogue program was also organized in the DFPD on 23rd September 2026. On this occasion, officials of the department actively participated, shared ideas, and further strengthened the resolve for cleanliness. In the program Smt. Abha Kumar, Sr. Vice President, Sulabh International Social Service Organization, shared her views on the importance of cleanliness.

On the occasion of Swachhata Hi Seva-2025, the officials of the Department visited market area nearby Krishi Bhawan on 24.09.2025 to promote Swachhata awareness and advocate for clean public spaces. The market area was cleaned, and dustbins were distributed to street vendors to encourage proper waste disposal and maintain cleanliness.

The Department also organized a Health check-up camp at Krishi Bhawan on 24.09.2026 in association with MASSH Super Specialty Hospital, New Delhi with their team of Senior Doctors including lab technicians. In the camp, various tests like blood sugar, Blood pressure etc. for Safai Mitras/Security Guards and Officials were conducted to ensure their well-being.

A Poem recitation competition on the theme "Swachhata Mein Sahbhag, Swachh Bharat, Viksit Bharat” was organized on 25.09.2026 in which the officials of DFPD participated.

Meanwhile the following activities have also been undertaken by the PSUs and Attached offices of the Department: -

On 22.09.2026, officers and employees of the Food Corporation of India (FCI) Headquarters and RO Maharashtra, RO Odisha, RO Haryana, organized a Swachhata Rally as part of the Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 Campaign. During the rally, participants actively engaged in cleanliness activities in the surrounding areas, markets and other public places along the route.

Cleanliness drive at public places such as hospitals, schools, roads etc. on 22.09.2026 by QCCs.

Awareness programmes for employees and young staff were organized on 23.09.2026 across all FCI offices, including Headquarters, Regional Offices, Divisional Offices, and Depots. These activities included Essay Writing Competitions, Poster-Making and Wall-Painting Competitions, Quizzes, and Slogan-Writing Competitions focused on cleanliness and sanitation. The activities encouraged collective efforts towards realizing the vision of a clean, hygienic, and sustainable India.

As part of the Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 campaign, Food Corporation of India (FCI) Headquarters and its subordinate offices, including Regional Offices, Divisional Offices and Depots, organised on 24.09.2026, awareness camps and outreach activities at nearby Government Schools and Anganwadi Centres across the country. The initiatives focused on nurturing the values of cleanliness, hygiene, sanitation and responsible waste-management practices among children.

IGMRI Ludhiana organised a “Neki Ki Deewar” on 24.09.2026 for the collection and reuse of usable clothes, promoting cleanliness, reuse and community welfare under “Swachhata Hi Seva-2026”.

Through these initiatives, the Department of Food and Public Distribution and its associated organisations continue to encourage active participation among employees, citizens and communities in promoting cleanliness, sanitation, hygiene and responsible waste management, contributing towards the vision of a Swachh Bharat and Viksit Bharat.

headline: Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal to Visit the United States to Participate in G20 Trade Ministers’ Meeting
fullText:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry

Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal to Visit the United States to Participate in G20 Trade Ministers’ Meeting

Shri Goyal to Engage With Leaders of American Industry, Investors and The Startup Community in Milwaukee, Chicago and New York

28 SEP 2026 6:19PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal will visit the United States of America from 29 September to 5 October 2026. Shri Goyal will participate in the G20 Trade Ministers’ Meeting to be held in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, on 30 September and 1 October 2026, at the invitation of the U.S. Trade Representative (USTR).

The Meeting will bring together Trade Ministers of G20 members. India will engage constructively with all G20 members and work towards a rules-based, open, inclusive, transparent, equitable and non-discriminatory multilateral trading system, with the World Trade Organization at its core, while ensuring adequate policy space for developing countries. On the sidelines of the Meeting, Shri Goyal will hold bilateral meetings with his counterparts. The engagements will focus on expanding opportunities for farmers, fishermen, women entrepreneurs, startups, MSMEs and other enterprises.

Shri Piyush Goyal will also engage bilaterally with his counterpart from the United States as part of ongoing efforts to advance a balanced and mutually beneficial India-U.S. Bilateral Trade Agreement (BTA) and finalise an interim deal in line with the Joint Statement of 7 February 2026.

In Milwaukee and Chicago, Shri Goyal will meet chief executives of leading American companies in manufacturing, consumer goods, agri-business, retail and technology, and participate in roundtables with businesses, startups and innovative companies. He will highlight the opportunities India offers as a manufacturing and investment destination and invite American companies to deepen their partnerships with Indian enterprises.

In Chicago, Shri Goyal will pay floral tributes to Mahatma Gandhi on Gandhi Jayanti and Swami Vivekananda. He will also interact with professional associations representing the Indian community.

The visit is expected to further strengthen the trade and investment partnership between India and the United States and deepen India’s engagement with its G20 partners.

headline: Second India-Fiji Bilateral Joint Working Group Meeting Held in New Delhi
fullText:
Ministry of Defence

Second India-Fiji Bilateral Joint Working Group Meeting Held in New Delhi

28 SEP 2026 6:11PM by PIB Delhi

The second India–Fiji Bilateral Joint Working Group (JWG) meeting was held in New Delhi on September 28, 2026.The two countries held discussions on a wide range of areas of mutual interest, including military training and capacity building, service-to-service engagements, maritime security, cyber training, defence industry collaboration and enhanced institutional cooperation between the Armed Forces of India and Fiji.

India reiterated the importance accorded to Fiji and the Pacific Island Countries in its vision of a free, open, inclusive and secure Indo-Pacific. Both sides expressed satisfaction at the growing bilateral defence engagements and reaffirmed their commitment to further expanding cooperation in mutually beneficial areas.

The meeting was co-chaired by Shri Amitabh Prasad, Joint Secretary (International Cooperation), Ministry of Defence and Mr. Mason Smith, Permanent Secretary for Defence & Veterans Affairs, Fiji. Mr. Smith also met Defence Secretary Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh on the sidelines of the 2nd India–Fiji Bilateral Joint Working Group Meeting. Discussions focused on strengthening bilateral defence and maritime cooperation, including opportunities for greater defence industry collaboration.

As part of efforts to expand specialised military training cooperation, the Fijian delegation is scheduled to visit Kochi on 29–30 September 2026. The delegation will inspect facilities at the Southern Naval Command to formalise advanced naval training cooperation and professional aviation training modules, enhancing technical proficiency and operational synergy between the two maritime forces.

Prior to the commencement of the official bilateral talks, Mr. Smith paid solemn tribute to India's fallen soldiers at the National War Memorial, New Delhi. The Fijian delegation also visited the DPSU Bhavan at the World Trade Centre, New Delhi, where it was briefed on India's indigenous defence manufacturing capabilities. The visit highlighted advancements under the 'Aatmanirbhar Bharat' initiative, with a focus on exhibition displays and advanced Augmented Reality/Virtual Reality (AR/VR) simulation facilities that replicate real-world battlefield conditions.

India and Fiji share close and friendly relations, underpinned by historical, cultural and people-to-people ties. The meeting provided an opportunity to consolidate the existing defence partnership and identify new avenues for cooperation. Both sides agreed to maintain regular engagements and work towards further deepening bilateral defence cooperation.

headline: Ministry of Steel Announces Apex Body for Strengthening Safety Standards and improve safety culture in Steel sector
fullText:
Ministry of Steel

Ministry of Steel Announces Apex Body for Strengthening Safety Standards and improve safety culture in Steel sector

28 SEP 2026 6:10PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Steel, Government of India, has decided to set up a Steel Industry Safety Council (SISC) as an apex-level industry safety body under the administrative control of the Ministry of Steel. The initiative is aimed at strengthening safety standards, practices, accident prevention and safety awareness across the steel industry.

The Council will be headed by the Secretary, Ministry of Steel, as Chairman and will include senior officials of the Ministry, Chief Executives of integrated steel producers, and representatives of key technical and statutory organisations including the Directorate General of Mines Safety (DGMS), Petroleum and Explosives Safety Organisation (PESO), National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) and recognised steel technology institutions.

The SISC will assess the safety situation in the steel industry, facilitate studies and improvements in safety practices, approve industry safety standards and recommended practices, and review serious accidents, accidents and near-miss incidents. It will also provide directions for strengthening safety awareness, training and preventive measures.

To provide technical and professional support to the Council, a Steel Industry Safety Directorate (SISD) will be established. The Directorate will have expertise in areas including process safety, blast furnaces, steel melting, rolling mills, coke ovens, refractory systems, electrical and mechanical safety, occupational health, fire engineering and disaster management.

The SISD will oversee implementation of the Council's decisions, undertake periodic safety audits and reviews, maintain and disseminate accident and near-miss information, conduct investigations into serious safety incidents, review emergency preparedness and safety training programmes, and develop and issue Steel Industry Safety Standards, Recommended Practices and Guidelines suited to Indian conditions.

The establishment of SISC and SISD represents an important institutional step towards promoting a stronger safety culture, improving prevention of industrial accidents and advancing consistent safety practices across India's steel industry.

headline: Union Minister Shri Shivraj Chouhan Calls for Data-Driven Planning, Timely Procurement and Scientific Monitoring for Rabi Season 2026
fullText:
Ministry of Agriculture &

Union Minister Shri Shivraj Chouhan Calls for Data-Driven Planning, Timely Procurement and Scientific Monitoring for Rabi Season 2026

Shri Chouhan Launches Rabi Campaign 2026, Calls for Climate-Resilient Agriculture Roadmap

Union Agriculture Minister Calls for Water-Based Crop Planning, Stronger Preparedness for Rabi 2026

Pulses and Oilseeds to Drive Rabi Strategy as Shri Chouhan Pushes for Greater Self-Reliance

From Seed to Market, States Must Ensure Timely Inputs and Assured Procurement: Union Agriculture Minister

Shri Chouhan Calls for Weekly Crop Monitoring, Balanced Fertiliser Use and Stronger Farmer Support

28 SEP 2026 5:57PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare and Rural Development, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan, today called upon States to complete preparations for the Rabi season through coordinated planning, scientific assessment and close field-level monitoring. Addressing the two-day National Agriculture Conference – Rabi Campaign 2026 in New Delhi, he said that amid climate change, erratic rainfall and water constraints, food security and higher farm incomes would require data-driven planning and stronger Centre-State coordination rather than conventional approaches. The conference, organised by the Department of Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare at the Bharat Ratna C. Subramaniam Auditorium, NASC Complex, Pusa, was attended by Union Ministers of State for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare Shri Ram Nath Thakur and Shri Bhagirath Choudhary, Secretary, Department of Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare, Shri Atish Chandra, Director General, ICAR, Dr. M.L. Jat, senior officials from the Centre and States, Principal Secretaries and Directors of Agriculture, Vice-Chancellors of State Agricultural Universities, heads of ICAR institutes, and representatives of KVKs, ATMA and other stakeholders. In his inaugural address, Shri Chouhan said Rabi 2026 is an important phase in advancing the vision of a self-reliant and developed India. The conference, he said, is aimed at strengthening Centre-State coordination, raising agricultural production and productivity, promoting sustainability and preparing a coordinated, outcome-oriented strategy for enhancing farmers’ incomes.

Water Budget Must Guide Crop Planning

Shri Chouhan identified the water budget as one of the most important parameters for Rabi planning, asking every State and district to assess the water available for irrigation before finalising crop plans. Areas with limited water availability should prioritise less water-intensive crops such as pulses and oilseeds, while areas with assured irrigation can plan other crops accordingly. He said rainfall has remained below normal, although not to an extent that would severely affect water availability at the national level. However, water shortages in some States remain a concern. States must assess water availability and soil moisture in vulnerable areas and make arrangements for irrigation in advance. “There should be no situation where a crop requiring more water is sown and adequate water is subsequently unavailable, resulting in crop losses,” he said, stressing that preparations must begin immediately as the Rabi sowing window is approaching. Rainfed areas, in particular, require careful planning as the availability of soil moisture largely determines the crop choice and outcome.

Centre to Undertake Ground Assessment of Drought-Hit Areas

Expressing concern over drought conditions in Maharashtra and Karnataka, Shri Chouhan said nearly two-thirds of Maharashtra has been affected and the State has declared drought, while Karnataka is also facing drought-like conditions. He said a Central team would undertake a ground assessment in Karnataka on October 3, while a Central team would also be sent to Maharashtra. Shri Chouhan said he would personally visit the affected States with his team and assured that, under the leadership and guidance of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Central Government stands firmly with farmers during the difficult situation. He also said that Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh would need crop plans based on water availability and soil moisture. Separate strategies should be prepared for rainfed and irrigated areas. Delayed sowing, he cautioned, can affect germination as well as productivity, making timely sowing and advance preparation essential.

Timely Availability of Quality Seed a Key Priority

Calling seed the most critical link in Rabi preparations, Shri Chouhan asked States to determine immediately which varieties are best suited to specific regions and agro-climatic conditions. He expressed concern that some States neither place seed demands in adequate time nor lift the required quantities, resulting in delays in distribution. In some cases, valuable seed varieties reach farmers after the sowing window and are subsequently sold at prices comparable to ordinary grain. He called for a complete roadmap covering seed demand, procurement, lifting and distribution. With senior ICAR scientists and experts present at the conference, States should jointly identify the most suitable varieties for different regions and conditions. He also called for an assessment of which varieties released by agricultural institutions have gained adoption and which have not, followed by targeted farmer awareness and extension efforts. This exercise, he said, should be completed scientifically during the two-day conference.

Push for Pulses and Oilseeds, Backed by Assured Markets

Shri Chouhan urged States to promote pulses and oilseeds, particularly in areas that remain fallow after paddy cultivation. These crops require relatively less water and are central to the national objective of achieving self-reliance in pulses and edible oils. He asked every State to finalise by September 29 its Rabi plan indicating the area to be brought under pulses and the crops to be promoted, including chana, masoor and mustard. At the same time, he stressed that production planning must be accompanied by assured market arrangements. Farmers should have confidence that their produce will be procured on time. “If there are areas where nothing is grown after paddy, this is an opportunity to encourage farmers to take up pulses,” he said, calling for immediate action by the States.

Procurement Planning Must Be in Place in Advance

Shri Chouhan said procurement arrangements must be planned alongside production so that farmers have confidence in the market. If State governments are unable to undertake procurement on time, Central nodal agencies NAFED and NCCF will undertake direct procurement from farmers. However, States must provide the necessary support, including timely facilitation of mandi-related requirements and other arrangements, to ensure that procurement is not delayed. He said the Centre has approved proposals on a large scale for procurement of pulses and oilseeds under the Price Support Scheme (PSS) and urged States to make full use of the mechanism. He also pointed out that some States submit procurement proposals but subsequently do not undertake the purchase. States, therefore, must prepare a complete procurement roadmap covering seed availability, distribution, production and market arrangements. Shri Chouhan also suggested that States consult farmers while preparing seed plans and make effective use of the network of Krishi Vigyan Kendras.

Balanced Fertiliser Use and Expansion of ‘Khet Bachao Abhiyan’

Shri Chouhan called for greater emphasis on balanced use of fertilisers, noting that if one bag is sufficient for a crop, there is no reason to apply two. Excessive application raises cultivation costs and can affect soil health. He urged States to extend the ‘Khet Bachao Abhiyan’, launched during the Kharif season, to Rabi as well. He cited the experience of southern States where fertilizer use has declined without affecting production, and called for these experiences to be shared and replicated. States should encourage farmers to adopt balanced fertiliser application with support from agricultural scientists, he said, adding that the Centre is ready to provide scientific assistance wherever required. Shri Chouhan also stressed the need for timely availability and distribution of fertilisers. Just as seed must reach farmers before sowing, fertilisers must also be available at the right time. He referred to pilot initiatives based on Farmer ID to strengthen distribution and ensure that fertilisers reach genuine farmers while preventing diversion and black marketing. He said the Centre is currently spending around ₹2 lakh crore on fertiliser subsidy, while farmers continue to receive fertilisers at subsidised prices, including urea at ₹266 per bag and DAP at ₹1,350 per bag. Ensuring balanced use of this subsidised input, he said, is also a responsibility of the States. The ‘Khet Bachao Abhiyan’, he said, is not only about reducing excessive fertilizer use but also about protecting soil health, beneficial organisms and the productive capacity of farmland for future generations.

Natural Farming: Focus on Branding, Marketing and Certification

Shri Chouhan said farmers are increasingly prepared to adopt natural farming and registration has also progressed, but States must now focus on branding and marketing of natural farm products. Citing Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat and Himachal Pradesh, he said these States have developed brands for natural farming products and established their market identity, helping them command better prices. States should also ensure that certification does not become a barrier for farmers and that natural products receive appropriate market recognition.

Farmer Credit Card and Farmer ID Need Greater Coverage

Shri Chouhan said around 9.54 crore farmer families have been covered under the PM-KISAN scheme, but the coverage of Kisan Credit Cards remains inadequate in several areas, particularly among small and marginal farmers. He asked States to identify areas where KCC coverage remains low and examine bottlenecks in loan sanctioning at the banking level so that farmers can access credit in time for agricultural investment. He clarified that the objective is not to push farmers towards borrowing, but to ensure that farmers who need timely capital for agriculture have access to institutional credit. On Farmer ID and AgriStack, Shri Chouhan congratulated States for the progress made and called for completing the remaining work at a faster pace, including land parcel-related work. A robust digital foundation, he said, will help resolve farmers’ problems and enable more efficient delivery of government schemes. He also stressed that tenant farmers and farmers cultivating land at different locations must not be left out of the Farmer ID framework and called for coordinated efforts to bring them into the system.

Weekly Monitoring of Crops, Disease and Market Prices

Shri Chouhan called for weekly monitoring in every State of crop conditions, sowing progress, germination, pest and disease attacks and market prices. He said real-time information would enable authorities to identify emerging problems and take corrective action without delay. The Agriculture Department and relevant agencies should maintain close surveillance of the situation on the ground. He said the Ministry also conducts weekly reviews at the national level covering crop conditions, market rates and disease outbreaks, enabling timely intervention wherever required.

On this occasion, Secretary, Department of Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare, Shri Atish Chandra emphasised that, amid changing weather patterns, uneven rainfall and moisture-related challenges in rainfed areas, it is essential to promote agricultural diversification, sustainable farming and research-based agricultural practices.

He further emphasised the need to take concrete steps to enhance farmers’ incomes and realise the goal of self-reliant agriculture through initiatives such as ‘Per Drop More Crop’, soil health management, modern agricultural infrastructure, robust market mechanisms and digital agriculture solutions, ensuring their reach to the last mile.

Secretary, DARE and Director General, ICAR, Dr. Mangi Lal Jat in his address identified self-reliance, crop diversification, climate-resilient and sustainable agriculture, digital agriculture, and risk mitigation as key priorities for the upcoming Rabi campaign. He emphasised promoting oilseed and pulse production, with a special focus on crop diversification through targeted strategies in rice-fallow areas. He said that this would require the development of a comprehensive technological package covering everything from crop and suitable variety selection to quality seeds, mechanisation, biological solutions and seed treatment.

Dr. Jat informed that during the upcoming season, large-scale demonstrations of green ammonia are planned across 10,000 acres in 37 districts of six states.

Two-Day Conference to Shape Rabi Action Plan

The two-day National Agriculture Conference brings together senior officials from the Centre and States, ICAR scientists and the Agriculture Ministry’s teams. The first day will feature three rounds of thematic group discussions covering self-reliance and diversification; sustainability and climate-resilient agriculture; and digital agriculture, infrastructure, financing and risk management. On September 29, Shri Chouhan will hold detailed discussions with Agriculture Ministers of the States. The deliberations will cover the weather outlook for the Rabi season, fertiliser availability, the Digital Agriculture Mission, Farmer Registry, missions on pulses and edible oils, the PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana, marketing reforms, and planning through ATMA and KVKs, among other issues. The concluding session will consolidate the outcomes of the discussions and prepare a robust action plan for increasing Rabi production, empowering farmers and advancing the vision of a self-reliant and developed India. Agriculture Ministers from the States will also have an opportunity to share their experiences, priorities and suggestions on agricultural development and Rabi preparedness. Inputs from the States and the outcomes of the thematic discussions are expected to contribute to a coordinated and outcome-oriented strategy for Rabi Campaign 2026.

headline: Ministry of Mines Strengthens E-Waste Collection Drive under Special Campaign 6 to Promote Circular Economy and Critical Mineral Recovery
fullText:
Ministry of Mines

Ministry of Mines Strengthens E-Waste Collection Drive under Special Campaign 6 to Promote Circular Economy and Critical Mineral Recovery

28 SEP 2026 5:37PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Mines, Government of India, is strengthening its E-Waste Collection Campaign under Special Campaign 6 with a focus on responsible e-waste management, resource recovery and promotion of a circular economy.

The campaign is being coordinated and implemented through the Jawaharlal Nehru Aluminium Research Development and Design Centre (JNARDDC), Nagpur, designated as the Nodal Agency for the campaign, in association with the Material Recycling Association of India (MRAI). Collection and awareness activities are being undertaken at multiple locations by offices and organisations associated with the Ministry of Mines.

More than 44 office locations across the country have been finalised for the campaign. In Maharashtra alone, more than 28 locations have been identified for e-waste collection. The widespread participation of offices and organisations reflects the coordinated efforts being undertaken to promote responsible collection and disposal of e-waste. The Ministry of Mines office in New Delhi is also one of the identified collection locations under the campaign. E-waste collected at various participating locations will be channelised for responsible recycling and resource recovery through appropriate mechanisms.

E-waste is not merely a waste stream but also a potential source of valuable secondary resources. With several electronic products containing minerals and metals that are important for modern technologies, recycling and recovery from e-waste can contribute to resource efficiency and strengthen the circular economy for critical minerals. Responsible recycling can help recover valuable materials, reduce pressure on primary mineral resources and promote sustainable utilisation of resources.

As part of the preparatory activities for effective implementation of the campaign, JNARDDC has conducted virtual coordination meetings with designated Nodal Officers of various offices and organisations under the Ministry of Mines, including the Geological Survey of India (GSI), Indian Bureau of Mines (IBM), National Institute of Rock Mechanics (NIRM), National Aluminium Company Limited (NALCO), Hindustan Zinc Limited (HZL), Mineral Exploration and Consultancy Limited (MECL) and Hindustan Copper Limited (HCL).

The Ministry and its field offices and organisations are also undertaking awareness activities, campaigns and competitions to encourage greater participation among employees and stakeholders. These activities aim to promote awareness about responsible e-waste disposal and encourage reuse, repurposing and recycling of discarded electronic and electrical products, wherever feasible.

Through the campaign, the Ministry is promoting Jan Bhagidari in resource conservation and encouraging responsible practices for the collection, segregation, recycling and recovery of materials from e-waste. The initiative also reinforces the broader objectives of Special Campaign 6 towards sustainable resource management, environmental responsibility and a circular economy.

Indian Railways Approves ₹122 Crore for 6 km Barbil–Bolanikhadan Doubling Project of South Eastern Railway

Doubling to Support Growing Iron Ore Movement, Strengthen Mineral Corridor and Address Future Capacity Requirements

28 SEP 2026 5:32PM by PIB Delhi

Indian Railways has approved the 6 km Barbil-Bolanikhadan Doubling Project of South Eastern Railway at a completion cost of ₹122 crore, strengthening rail infrastructure on an important mineral movement corridor.

Doubling to Support Growing Freight Traffic

The project will facilitate additional freight traffic of 8.9 MTPA on this stretch after commissioning of the project. The doubling will also help reduce delays to freight trains.

The Barbil-Bolanikhadan section has been identified under the “Energy, Mineral and Cement Corridor” of Indian Railways. The existing section is a single-line section and currently carries about 9 MTPA, comprising about 6 loaded rakes per day of originating iron ore traffic. The traffic is entirely for high-grade ore and pellets moving from SAIL’s Bolani mines and private sidings (Rungta, Khatau Narbheram) to major steel plants and ports.

Meeting Future Freight Requirements

Doubling this 6 km stretch, ahead of the full realisation of SAIL’s mine expansion and port/plant capacity additions, will help to prevent the capacity constraints in the designated mineral corridor.

The approved work will support the growing freight requirements, improve rail connectivity for movement of iron ore to steel plants and ports, and strengthen rail capacity as mining, industrial and port activities expand in the region. It will also strengthen the Energy, Mineral and Cement Corridor and support smoother movement of freight on this important route.

headline: From Financial Hardship to Academic Achievement
fullText:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment

From Financial Hardship to Academic Achievement

Telangana Woman Smt Yatla Sravanthi’s Journey through NFSC

28 SEP 2026 5:23PM by PIB Delhi

Timely institutional assistance can help scholars overcome these barriers, continue their academic journeys and contribute to higher education and research. Otherwise, the financial constraints and limited access to educational resources can prevent deserving students from pursuing higher education and advanced research.

Smt. Yatla Sravanthi, a 37-year-old resident of Karimnagar district, Telangana, successfully completed her research in Botany with financial assistance under the National Fellowship for Scheduled Caste (NFSC) Scheme. Her fellowship assistance began in 2017, and she availed support in the form of fellowship, House Rent Allowance and contingency assistance amounting to Rs. 21 lakh.

Before receiving assistance, Smt. Sravanthi faced severe financial difficulties in continuing her higher education and doctoral research. Her family’s financial situation made it difficult to meet expenses related to books, research materials, equipment and hostel accommodation. These constraints affected her ability to focus fully on her studies and research.

She also faced limited access to quality educational resources, internet facilities and appropriate academic guidance. Coming from a remote area and facing social and economic disadvantages, pursuing doctoral-level education was particularly challenging. Without financial support, she could have been compelled to take loans or interrupt her education to seek employment.

The NFSC Scheme provided Smt. Sravanthi with financial stability and enabled her to devote greater time and attention to her doctoral research. The monthly fellowship helped reduce the economic burden associated with her education and living expenses, while the contingency assistance enabled her to procure essential books, research materials and software required for her academic work.

The fellowship also enabled her to participate in national seminars and workshops. These opportunities allowed her to present her research findings, interact with experts, receive academic feedback and develop professional networks. Such exposure strengthened her academic experience and broadened her access to the research community.

With the support of the NFSC Scheme, Smt. Sravanthi was able to pursue her research with greater confidence and complete her academic work. The fellowship strengthened her research profile and created opportunities for professional interaction and networking. At a personal level, the reduction in financial pressure on her family brought greater confidence and independence.

INDIAN NAVY TO HOST SECOND EDITION OF COMMANDERS’ CONFERENCE 2026 AT NAUSENA BHAWAN, NEW DELHI

28 SEP 2026 5:15PM by PIB Delhi

The Commanders’ Conference 2026/02 (the second edition of 2026 Indian Navy’s biannual Conference) is scheduled over a period of three days from 29 Sep 2026 to 01 Oct 2026 at Nausena Bhawan, New Delhi. As the Navy’s Apex Level forum, the Conference provides an avenue for senior Naval leadership, including outstation Operational and Area Commanders, to undertake a comprehensive review of Operational preparedness at the military-strategic level and engage with Senior Government functionaries through an institutionalised mechanism.

The Conference will be pivotal in underscoring Indian Navy’s contribution towards safeguarding India’s maritime interests, including ‘Security of Energy’ amidst the ongoing conflicts in West Asia. The Navy’s resolute conduct of the ongoing Operation Urja Suraksha and its emergence as a credible maritime force further bolsters its stature as a Preferred Security Partner in the Indian Ocean Region and beyond.

On the Opening Day, Hon’ble Raksha Mantri will share his vision and guidance on national maritime perspectives and expectations from Indian Navy. The Chief of the Defence Staff and the Chief of the Army Staff will also engage with Naval Commanders to foster tri-Services synergy and integration.

On subsequent days, Chief of the Naval Staff, along with the Commanders-in-Chief, will review key focus areas namely Operations, Materiel, Logistics, HR, Training, induction of niche technologies such as AI, Big Data Analysis (BDA), Autonomous/Uncrewed Systems, and Cyber Operations, reinforcing the need to imbibe cutting-edge warfighting concepts and accelerating technology absorption.

On a broader canvas, the Navy’s apex leadership will assess overall preparedness to optimise force levels and enhance combat readiness in consonance with three foundational pillars of ‘JAI – Jointness, Aatmanirbharta, Innovation’, in pursuit of the GoI’s vision of Aatmanirbharta and Viksit Bharat 2047.

The Indian Navy continues to maintain a high tempo of operations, steadfast on its course as a Combat Ready, Credible, Cohesive, and Future-Ready Force in the service of the nation.

headline: India Reaffirms Commitment to Conservation of Whales and Other Cetaceans at IWC-70 in Hobart, Australia
fullText:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

India Reaffirms Commitment to Conservation of Whales and Other Cetaceans at IWC-70 in Hobart, Australia

Science-based conservation, international cooperation and practical measures essential to address threats to cetaceans, stresses India

28 SEP 2026 5:10PM by PIB Delhi

India today underlined the need for conservation of whales and other cetaceans at the 70th meeting of the International Whaling Commission (IWC-70), being held in Hobart, Australia, from 28.09.2026 to 02.10.2026.

In its Opening Statement at IWC-70, India emphasized the importance of continued collaboration among range countries, scientific institutions and relevant international organisations for effective cetacean conservation. India highlighted that improved scientific information on population status, distribution, movements, breeding ecology and threats is essential for strengthening conservation measures and supporting informed decision-making.

India reaffirmed its support for scientific studies and evidence-based approaches to ensure that the conservation and management of cetaceans remain grounded in sound scientific understanding. It also emphasized the importance of greater cooperation among governments, researchers and local communities in developing practical and locally appropriate approaches to address threats to cetaceans.

The meeting assumes special significance as it coincides with the 80th anniversary of the signing of the International Convention for the Regulation of Whaling.

The International Whaling Commission (IWC) was set up under the International Convention for the Regulation of Whaling, signed in Washington DC on 02.12.1946, as the global body responsible for management of whaling and conservation of whales. Its membership includes 89 governments from all over the world. India has been a member of the International Whaling Commission since 1981 and has played a proactive and prominent role in the conservation of whales.

Cetacean species occurring in Indian waters receive the highest level of legal protection under the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972. Several Marine Protected Areas have also been notified in the country to provide protection to the rich marine biodiversity, including whales, dolphins, dugongs, sharks, rays, turtles and corals.

The Government of India has further initiated Project Dolphin, adopting a holistic approach towards the conservation of dolphins, whales, porpoises and associated aquatic ecosystems. India also attaches particular importance to the conservation of the Arabian Sea humpback whale, which has been identified among the 25 species for focused conservation efforts.

India reiterated that the future work of the International Whaling Commission should continue to be guided by science-based conservation priorities, international cooperation and practical measures for addressing the diverse threats faced by whales and other cetaceans.

headline: INDIAN COAST GUARD RESPONDS TO MARITIME DISTRESS OFF PARADIP
fullText:
Ministry of Defence

INDIAN COAST GUARD RESPONDS TO MARITIME DISTRESS OFF PARADIP

STABILISES BELIZE-FLAGGED TANKER MT SEAGULL 9

28 SEP 2026 5:00PM by PIB Delhi

The Indian Coast Guard (ICG) successfully averted a major maritime incident following a distress situation onboard the Belize-flagged chemical tanker MT Seagull 9, approximately 37 nautical miles East-South-East of Paradip, Odisha.

The vessel, carrying 9,000 metric tonnes of palm oil with 23 crew members onboard, issued an urgent distress call at approximately 0730 hrs on September 27, 2026 following main engine failure and rapid flooding of a ballast tank, resulting in a dangerous tilt of the vessel.

ICGS Vishwast was immediately deployed to the location. A specialist ICG Damage Control Team boarded the unstable vessel and commenced emergency damage-control measures. The team deployed submersible de-flooding pumps, arrested the leakage, blanked two damaged seawater pipelines, and contained a third fractured line, eliminating the threat of capsizing.

To augment the response, the Indian Coast Guard diverted a Pollution Control Vessel (PCV) and an additional Offshore Patrol Vessel (OPV). Simultaneously, ICG Dornier aircraft launched from Bhubaneswar for real-time aerial surveillance. A minor palm-oil sheen initially observed near the vessel on Sep 27, 2026 was confirmed fully dissipated during follow-up aerial sorties on September 28, 2026. Strict pollution-response protocols remain active to safeguard the marine ecosystem.

Following stabilisation, Paradip Port Authority tug Dolphin took MT Seagull 9 under tow towards the anchorage area off Paradip. ICGS Vishwast, along with the other deployed specialised assets, remains on scene, maintaining an active sentinel watch and providing continuous operational support.
